scope: Interface-preserving alternatives using pinned rayon-core 1.13.0; source inspection, not a proof that all safe implementations are exhausted
required_interface: Borrowed callbacks without a new static lifetime requirement
Calling participant executes on the invoking physical thread
Worker teardown without a new intentional registry leak

alternatives.evidence: src/thread_pool/mod.rs documents callback execution inside the target pool; install blocks an external invoking thread until completion.
alternatives.disposition: Not a drop-in replacement for concurrent participation on the invoking thread; internal worker-subtree install is already used by the candidate.

alternatives.candidate: ThreadPoolBuilder::use_current_thread to enable stack-backed caller joins
alternatives.evidence: src/lib.rs local-thread-pool documentation explicitly states the registry is leaked when using the current thread.
alternatives.disposition: Rejected for this migration: it introduces intentional lifecycle debt rather than resolving retention.

alternatives.evidence: src/thread_pool/mod.rs requires static callback lifetimes for asynchronous jobs.
alternatives.disposition: Rejected as a drop-in replacement: borrowed callbacks cannot satisfy that interface without changing caller requirements or reintroducing lifetime erasure.

alternatives.candidate: One shared pool with broadcast selecting only reserved indices
alternatives.evidence: src/thread_pool/mod.rs broadcast executes on every pool thread and completes after all threads finish.
alternatives.disposition: Rejected as a simple replacement: the selected free worker completed, but broadcast returned only after the unrelated busy worker was released. The bounded scheduler experiment passed 20 repeated executions.

broadcast_experiment.branch: experiment/87-broadcast-reservations (local throwaway branch, not part of the migration PR)
broadcast_experiment.runtime: Existing pinned Rayon release dependency; Rust 1.99.0, Linux x86_64
broadcast_experiment.assertions: Free participant signaled completion; broadcast result channel remained empty while busy participant was held; broadcast completed after release.
broadcast_experiment.bound: Five-second event waits plus an external fifteen-second process timeout; all 20 repeated runs exited successfully.
broadcast_experiment.limits: This rejects the direct broadcast substitution, not every possible shared-pool design. No production dispatch was changed.

follow_up: scoped-pool-alternatives.md examines four established scoped/thread-pool interfaces; none establishes a compatible lower-cost replacement. This is not an impossibility proof.
next_step: Resolve resource-budget direction or demonstrate a further compatible executor before implementation; do not weaken reservation semantics to reduce allocation counts.
